data.content_ref: inline:The 'shared mechanism' is defined so generically that it fails to identify a shared *mechanism* — it reduces to 'any signal causally coupled to reasoning structure can break outcome-equivalence.' But this is a category, not a mechanism: it does not specify the causal pathway by which *both* internal observables (explanation quality) and external observables (OOD accuracy) are produced by the same underlying generative process. The named signals — response times, intermediate judgments, OOD accuracy — plausibly arise from different cognitive or computational substrates, so asserting they share a single mechanism without specifying the common causal architecture is an unsupported abstraction. The stated refutation condition (dissociation between process traces and OOD accuracy) is in fact *plausible by default* given they measure different aspects, yet the target treats the shared mechanism as established rather than as the very claim under test.
